outcome: A August 2026 preprint by Ivan Dynnikov proves a structural reduction of the Zeeman collapsibility conjecture (ZCC): any counterexample to ZCC would yield a 'standard' counterexample, and ZCC holds for polyhedra embeddable in 3-manifolds; the general conjecture remains open, and no case of it (in the sense of a class of complexes previously undecided) was settled outright.

summary: Since 26 January 2024, no resolution, partial case, or counterexample to Zeeman's collapsibility conjecture (ZCC) has appeared. The most substantial development is Ivan Dynnikov's preprint 'On Zeeman's collapsibility conjecture for non-standard polyhedra' (arXiv:2608.23331, submitted 24 August 2026), which proves that (Theorem 2.5/1.4) any compact contractible 2-dimensional polyhedron can be transformed via 3-deformability moves into a 'semi-standard' polyhedron, so that if a counterexample to ZCC exists at all, a standard one exists; it also shows (Theorem 1.5) ZCC holds for polyhedra embeddable in 3-manifolds, leaning on the (proven) Poincare-Perelman theorem. This is a genuine narrowing of where a counterexample could be found for the exact problem as stated (contractible 2-complex K, is K x [0,1] collapsible?) — it is about the same object, not a variant — but it does not decide any previously-open sub-case in either direction: standard polyhedra were already the hardest and most-studied case, and the reduction leaves the truth value of ZCC on those exactly as open as before. I therefore classify this as 'progress' rather than 'partial': the theorem narrows the search space (akin to a bound moving) rather than settling a restriction of the stated question. The paper itself flags that part of its argument (a transfer of Matveev's 1987 technique to a new case) is asserted rather than independently re-verified, which the triage record also flagged as worth checking. Separately, a December 2024 preprint by Fagan, Qiu and Wang, 'Stable Andrews-Curtis Conjecture via Fake Surfaces and Zeeman Conjecture' (arXiv:2412.12293), relates the stable Andrews-Curtis conjecture to a reformulation via 'fake surfaces' and proves a small case (complexity < 6) of that reformulation; this is about the stable Andrews-Curtis conjecture, a related but distinct problem, not a case of ZCC itself, so it does not count as a change to this bullet and I treat it as background context only. No AI system played any role in either paper's mathematics: the Dynnikov preprint explicitly discloses that Google Gemini's web version was used 'solely for the purpose of final language editing,' which is exactly the kind of contribution (proofreading/tidying) that these codes classify as ai_role 'none'. No search turned up any AI lab announcement, LLM-produced proof or counterexample, or withdrawn AI claim concerning the Zeeman conjecture specifically (distinct AI results exist for other named problems, e.g. the unit distance conjecture and Jacobian conjecture, found incidentally while searching, but those are unrelated problems and not applicable here).
competing_reading: One could argue Dynnikov's Theorem 1.5 (ZCC holds for polyhedra embeddable in 3-manifolds) is a genuine 'case settled' and thus warrants status 'partial' rather than 'progress', since it restricts the stated question (all contractible 2-complexes) to a concrete sub-class (those embeddable in 3-manifolds) and answers it affirmatively. Under a stricter reading of §3.1 ('a case of the problem... settling it removes territory from the original... normally partial'), this would push the record to 'partial' with resolution_direction 'confirmed' for that sub-case. I lean 'progress' because the practical content of the paper is understood by the author primarily as a reduction/scope-narrowing result (the abstract and framing emphasize the standard/non-standard reduction, with the 3-manifold-embeddable case presented as a corollary of a lemma relying on the unverified Matveev transfer), but this is a genuinely close call.
what_would_settle_it: An expert digestion (e.g. a survey, MathOverflow discussion, or citation with commentary from a topologist) characterizing whether Theorem 1.5 is regarded by the community as a real settled sub-case of ZCC or merely a technical corollary en route to the main reduction; also, verification of whether Dynnikov's reliance on 'transfer of Matveev's technique' has been checked by anyone since posting.
